locator: I q.2 a.3 ad 1: nullo modo sineret aliquid mali esse in operibus suis, nisi esset adeo omnipotens et bonus, ut bene faceret etiam de malo
interpretation: Reading C of the preceding Augustine quotation: would not permit evil unless so powerful and good as to do good even from evil. This records only the necessary capability condition on permission, with de malo understood generically/collectively. It does not formalize the full counterfactual force of sineret or the divine attributes. The fixed nonempty collection is not quantified into arbitrary subsets and there is no per-evil distribution. CanDrawGoodFromEvils says capability to produce some good, not an existing good witness or an actual productive event; it therefore must not be substituted for DrawsGoodFromEvils or the older per-evil DrawsGoodFrom. This is a separate weaker-in-content reading of the modal clause, not a claim that the final eliciat sentence expresses only capability. No God, evil or actual permission is inferred, and no net benefit, best world or individual justification follows.
